title: Decisive Coalition and Dictator
body_html:
Decisive Coalition and Dictator

A coalition $C \subseteq N$ is decisive for a social welfare function $F$ ([[social_choice.voting.swf]]) if it is decisive for every ordered pair of alternatives: $$ \forall a, b \in A,\ \mathrm{IsDecisiveFor}(F, C, a, b). $$

An individual $i \in N$ is a dictator exactly when their singleton coalition $\{i\}$ is decisive in this sense.

In Lean: SocialChoice.Voting.IsDecisive F C and the singleton specialization SocialChoice.Voting.SWF.IsDictator F i := IsDecisive F {i}.

This identification is the structural heart of the decisive-coalition proof of Arrow ([[social_choice.voting.arrow_of_unanimity_iia]]): the dictatorship conclusion ([[social_choice.voting.dictatorial_swf]]) reduces to producing a singleton decisive coalition.

References

  • [MSZ 21.15] Maschler, Solan, and Zamir, Game Theory. Decisive coalitions and the singleton dictator.

lean_refs.name: SocialChoice.Voting.IsDecisive
lean_refs.signature:
def IsDecisive [Fintype N] [Fintype A] (F : SWF N A) (C : Set N) : Prop :=
  ∀ a b, IsDecisiveFor F C a b

lean_refs.name: SocialChoice.Voting.SWF.IsDictator
lean_refs.signature:
def SWF.IsDictator [Fintype N] [Fintype A] (F : SWF N A) (i : N) : Prop :=
  IsDecisive F {i}
